correctness.rationale: For any full Young subgroup, graph-edge orbits are exactly fixed edges among singleton labels, stars from one permuted block to one singleton, internal edges of one block, and complete bipartite edges between blocks. Internal orbits of blocks of size >=3 contain triangles, and between-block orbits contain four-cycles. For each block, distinct star orbits have a four-cycle and a size-two internal edge with a star has a triangle, so at most one eligible orbit per block. Conversely all permitted selections are a fixed-label forest with pendant/isolated trees, hence no further cycles. Equivariant barycentric coordinates give a canonical PL homeomorphism to the displayed join. Established matroid vertex decomposability and known forest Euler numbers yield every claimed sphere count and all exceptional cases. The independent finite verifier checks 14 block patterns and B_3..B_6 but is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The Young subgroups form a canonical and extensive family of symmetries of the basic complete-graph graphic matroid. A global PL decomposition of their *actual fixed-point spaces*, with exact integral sphere-wedge counts and empty/contractible/spherical boundaries, is substantial structural information not available from known ambient forest Euler tables or homology characters. Block-size stability for all sizes >=3 and the exceptional two-label block factor are natural consequences with independent equivariant-topological interest; the classification is infinite and does not depend on an arbitrary finite slice.
